summary: Dependency-confusion dropper under @servicetitan scope: preinstall downloads Bun and executes bundled 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a trivial ESLint processors stub (dist/index.js is ~15 lines) but ships a preinstall lifecycle script `node setup.mjs` that automatically runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh's GitHub releases into a temp directory and then invokes `execFileSync(bunBinary, [math_init.js])` against a bundled 727,680-byte file `math_init.js`. That file is a Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with hex-obfuscated identifiers, a rotated string/opcode array, and a `WV8StW` array-shuffler decoder consistent with the obfuscator.io shape. The advertised ESLint stub function does not require a second runtime or an opaque 727KB payload; the alternate runtime is used specifically to execute code that would otherwise be inspected by Node-focused tooling. The package is published under the `@servicetitan/` corporate scope with an empty description and a repository field pointing at `github.com/servicetitan/uikit.git` that does not correspond to a public package by this name — matching the dependency-confusion shape targeting ServiceTitan internal builds. On any machine or CI job that resolves this name, `npm install` auto-executes the obfuscated payload under the freshly-dropped Bun runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
